clue.text: Retire after defeat, as befits a boxer?

definitions.meaning: to withdraw and recover privately after being beaten
a fighter who has been hit tends his cuts after the bout, and a boxer dog would do so with its tongue

explanation.surface: Advice that a beaten fighter should quit the ring and recover.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means withdrawing to recover from a setback, literally what an injured animal or bruised fighter does.

clue.text: See poet in my, part of London planting tree.

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: the poet word sits inside the word my

parts.note: taken as written
a bard is a poet
Poplar is a district in East London

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a writer within a London district where trees are being planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the poet inside 'my'. Poplar is a district of East London, and 'planting' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lombardy poplar is a tall, narrow variety of poplar often planted in rows as a windbreak.

clue.text: League's accountant shows impatience when driving

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
a frustrated driver hoots the horn

explanation.surface: An association's bookkeeper is an impatient motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is to be in league or partnership, usually secretly.

clue.text: Prepared for a row, our heartless editor grabs article

indicators.note: the shortened word plus the editor take hold of the article inside them
heartless means the middle letter of the word our is dropped, keeping its outside letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Our editor, lacking spirit, seizes a piece in readiness for an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle letter of 'our'; the editor follows, and 'grabs' takes the article inside. 'Row' is the boating sense, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is fitted with oars is ready to be rowed; 'row' here is the boating sense, not a quarrel.

clue.text: Treasure in French film about initiator of robbery

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: the film's title goes around the opening letter of robbery

parts.note: Shine is a 1996 film about the pianist David Helfgott

indicators.note: the initiator of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A French heist film centred on the mastermind of a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps SHINE round R, the first letter given by 'initiator of robbery'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine something is to cherish it as sacred, so treasure works as a verb here.

clue.text: Who cut short dubious description of decaying matter?

indicators.note: the word Who loses its final letter, being docked at the end

parts.note: iffy means dubious or doubtful

explanation.surface: A question about who abbreviated a doubtful account of rotting stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last letter off WHO to leave WH.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiffy is British slang for smelly, which is how rotting material is described.

clue.text: Finished a lawsuit — characters starting sentences?

parts.note: time's up means time is finished
per means a, as in so much per week
a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A court action has been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives PER, as in 'ten pounds a head' meaning per head.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters, which open sentences, are called upper case from the printer's type tray.

clue.text: Favourite Australian river

definitions.meaning: a beloved or pet person, the apple of one's eye
a long river in south-east Australia

explanation.definitionFit: A cherished favourite is called this term of endearment, and it is also a major Australian river.

clue.text: Similarly, say, purchase an identical memento

indicators.note: say signals that the following word is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
a token is a memento, and the same means identical

explanation.surface: Someone buys a matching souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns BUY into its sound-alike BY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means likewise or for the same reason, a direct synonym of similarly.

clue.text: Overact, twirling new sari, greeting Hindu sage

indicators.note: twirling spins the overacting word round so it reads the other way

parts.note: to ham is to overact

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of sari are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A performer hams it up, spinning in a new sari to welcome a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twirling' turns HAM into MAH; 'new' rearranges SARI into ARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Maharishi is a title for a great Hindu teacher or seer.

clue.text: English composer's skilful evasion

definitions.meaning: Sir Hubert ... composed the setting of Jerusalem
a deft deflection of a blow or awkward question

explanation.surface: A musician known for his deft dodging.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubert Parry was the English composer of Jerusalem; a fencer's deflecting move is also this word.

clue.text: It's audibly granted to listeners

indicators.note: to listeners means the word is as heard, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: allowed means granted or permitted

explanation.surface: Something permitted by those who are listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to listeners' turns ALLOWED into ALOUD, a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken out loud means audibly, so that others can hear.

clue.text: Engineers initially find vessel is hard to re-equip

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word find

parts.note: an urn is a vessel
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Army engineers first locate a container that is difficult to restock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes F from 'find'.
explanation.definitionFit: To refurnish is to supply a room with new furniture, which means re-equipping it.

clue.text: Makes out album deserves to be heard

parts.note: a disc is a record album

indicators.note: to be heard signals that the word is spoken, so a sound-alike is entered

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out which record merits attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be heard' turns EARNS into ERNS, a sea eagle's name in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something out is to perceive or detect it, the sense of discerning.

clue.text: Like a burrowing creature originating on our planet

definitions.meaning: a fox or badger is born in an earth, its underground den
native to the world we live on

explanation.surface: A creature that tunnels and comes from this world.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal born in its den, called an earth, fits one sense; a mortal native to the globe fits the other.

clue.text: Old crone one's taken round good Scottish food

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman
one is I and the 's is 'is', so one's gives I and S

explanation.surface: An old woman has been driven around a fine Scottish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' puts IS around G to make IGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is Scotland's national dish of offal, oatmeal and spices.

clue.text: Law enforcers tuck in, not having dined

indicators.note: not having signals that a piece of the longer word is left out

parts.note: to interpolate is to insert or tuck in extra material
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Diners are told to start eating, though they have not eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck in' looks like an invitation to eat, but it means insert: INTERPOLATE, minus ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation coordinating forces across countries.

clue.text: Good person replacing centre of 10's cake

indicators.note: the good person takes the place of the middle letter of the answer to 10

parts.note: 10 across is the composer and evasion word
ST abbreviates saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A virtuous figure takes over the middle of a composer's cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing centre of' swaps the middle R of 10's answer for ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry is a small cake or baked confection made of dough.

clue.text: Initially so prolific, showing no originality

indicators.note: Initially takes just the opening letter of the word so

parts.note: lavish means abundant or prolific

explanation.surface: Something that starts out abundant ends up unoriginal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes S from 'so'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slavish copy follows its model exactly, without any independent creativity.

clue.text: Husband leaves song about Pooh's friend in vestibule

indicators.note: the shortened song wraps around the friend of Pooh
leaves signals that the husband abbreviation departs from the song

parts.note: an anthem is a song
Roo is the young kangaroo in Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A man walks out of a song about a Winnie-the-Pooh character in the hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops the husband from the song, leaving ANTEM, and 'about' wraps that round the young kangaroo from Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteroom is a small entrance chamber leading to a larger room, like a vestibule.

clue.text: Like the wind we get from the drink

definitions.text: Like the wind we get from the drink

parts.words: Like the wind we get from the drink
parts.note: the drink is crossword slang for the sea, so this describes a breeze blowing in off the sea towards land, not flatulence from alcohol

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about the gas that follows a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from the sea towards the land is called by this weather term.

clue.text: Curious afterthought about universal uproar

parts.note: rum means odd or curious

indicators.note: the afterthought letters go around the universal letter

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought in a letter
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: An odd postscript about something universal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PS round U to make PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion or disturbance.

clue.text: Engage in gambling in army theatre

parts.note: to play a game is to engage in it
house, or housey-housey, was the armed forces' name for the numbers game later called bingo

explanation.surface: Soldiers gambling while stationed in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: House was the army's gambling game, played for money: to play house is to engage in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a theatre, a building where plays are staged.

clue.text: About to pose for further examination

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Getting ready to pose again for another look.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a second attempt at a failed exam.

clue.text: Note about textile fibre

parts.note: ray (or re) is the second note of the sol-fa scale
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A memo concerning a kind of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a man-made fibre from cellulose used for fabric.

clue.text: Hispanic comrade Vespucci identified without hesitation

indicators.note: without signals that the hesitation sound is removed from the explorer's name

parts.note: Amerigo Vespucci was the explorer after whom America is named
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: An explorer recognised a Spanish-speaking friend without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identified' is a link word; 'without' takes ER out of AMERIGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, so it suits a Spanish-speaking companion.

clue.text: Cornfield plant an indicator of weather? Nonsense

parts.note: the red poppy grows wild among cereal crops
a weathercock shows the wind direction

explanation.surface: A wild flower that predicts the weather is a silly idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an indicator of weather' is a weathercock, shortened to COCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppycock is informal for rubbish or empty talk.

clue.text: It collapses readily, but Asians make light of it

definitions.meaning: a folding paper lamp flattens easily
a lamp from China gives light; 'make light of' usually means treat as trivial

explanation.surface: Something flimsy that people from the East do not take seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'but' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper lantern folds flat; the second reading is a lamp from China, also the name of a plant.
